The only known antidote is a mixture of atigax, klagul, megilloth and aldaka (which restores sight, removes the victim from a coma or reverses the effect of the poison if given within the first 12 rounds).
foragables.warning: The pink poison is easily discernible when applied to the edge of a blade

foragables.name: Madarch
foragables.characteristics: Madarch is a gaudy mushroom, purple in colour with a white underside and orange speckling. It is hard to miss because it reaches a maximum height of S' with a 4' diameter crown. Thin, succulent ridges run outward from the trunk on the underside of the crown. The hard, fibrous roots are only about I' in diameter, but more than strong enough to provide support for the fungus. In fact, they are so tough that a skilled axeman might have trouble felling one in less chan 10 minutes. Madarch grow in dark, damp, subterranean environments, usually in groups of 51-100.
foragables.medicinalUses: The thin ridges running outward from the underside of the crown contain a juice called norechor. Each giant mushroom yields a pint of norechor, which mixes with an equal portion of water to form a purple potion that warms the body and heals all of the imbiber’s cuts and damaged blood vessels within 2 hours.
foragables.otherUses: Madarch flesh is palatable and keeps for weeks on end; 1 lb can sustain a man for 3 days.
foragables.warning: If imbibed undiluted by water, norechor causes the blood to churn within its channels and swell with frightening fury. Unhealed wounds reopen and cuts widen. In some cases, a victim’s veins simply explode.

foragables.name: Madwort
foragables.characteristics: Madwort is an ugly, ground-hugging bush with spikes and (for most of the summer) small, yellowish flowers. Its greenish-yellow leaves may be mottled with brown spots and round in mountainous foothills on broken or stony ground.
foragables.otherUses:
The juice of madwort leaves may be boiled down to make a sticky paste which, when it impacts once it reaches its victim's bloodstream. If consumed, madwort poison is ½ as potent. The effects based on RR failure are
  • 1-25: induces madness for 11-20 rounds, causing him to tun about aimlessly, babble, attack friend and foe alike, etc.
  • 26-50: the poison inflicts 1-10 rounds of sensory disturbance, leaving the victim at -5O.
  • 51+: the resulting brain damage produce much more severe effects (10 to 20 points lost from the victim's potential Reasoning stat).

foragables.name: Mahal's Gift
foragables.characteristics: A species of little, silvery-blue, free-growing moss.
foragables.medicinalUses: When brewed into a tea and imbibed, the moss restores 50 concussion hits.

foragables.name: Maiana
foragables.characteristics: This plant is small, reaching only about 1' in height. It has several long, green-gold leaves with smooth edges, golden veins and white stems.
foragables.medicinalUses: When brewed into a tea, maiana cuts in half the dangerous effects of lung afflictions and respiratory disease. It keeps for up to a year, even though it dries out.

foragables.name: Malimmenté
foragables.characteristics: Malimmenté is tall (about 5") with long leaves, — resembling a stretched form of aloe. A common garden plant, it is somewhat rarer in the wild.
foragables.medicinalUses: Its leaves are crushed or applied in a poultice; it can also be dried or made into a salve that is only 25% as effective. Malimmenté is good for bruises, sprains, and pulled tendons and ligaments, reducing swelling and hastening recovery (2x normal rate).

foragables.name: Malodorous Milkcap
foragables.characteristics: This fungus boasts a small (S" in diameter), milky white cap with concentric rings of scales. This mushroom has an 18" stalk marked by black rings that exude a pungent foul odour, It usually grows in colonies well-known by any animals or persons living nearby.
foragables.otherUses: Small quantities of this mushroom may be eaten, but more than an ounce or two becomes mildly poisonous (2nd level paralytic)
foragables.warning: There is no antidote to the poison, but its effect wears off in 12 hours.

foragables.name: Margath
foragables.characteristics: This fungus resembles an orange, gelatinous kidney; it tends to grow as a solitary individual.
foragables.medicinalUses: Orcs concoct a healing salve from margath, a surface anaesthetic that replaces the pain of a wound with a steady burning sensation. The salve keeps for up to 6 months if kept in a closed container.
foragables.warning: Use of this fungus has the side effect of giving its consumer nightmares and a foul odour.

foragables.name: Megillos
foragables.characteristics: Megilloth lives underground in the form of a massive tuber; its visible, above-ground component is so small as to be dismissed out of hand as an insignificant weed: 3 limp, oval-shaped leaves, a short, brown stem, and spring flowers. It is found in rocky crags and ledges in the upper reaches of mountains.
foragables.otherUses: If eaten, megilloth’s bitter leaves increase visual perception (both in range and power) by S0-500% for a period of 10 minutes, If consumed after being roasted, the leaves double the range of vision for 4-8 hours. The megilloth root may be roasted so as to yield a tasty meal.
foragables.warning: If more than 1 leaf/day is consumed, the user experiences vertigo and hard pressed to remain standing (S0% chance) for 1 hour.

foragables.name: Melandar
foragables.characteristics: The bright green colour of this moss contrasts with the ice and snow it usually grows under, During the short growing season, it appears to become frosted with black soot, but these are only its spores. The rest of the year it lies dormant beneath the snow and ice. It is Light to find in Summer, but Extremely Hard any other time.
foragables.medicinalUses: If added to boiling water and simmered for 30 minutes, melandar produces a mild tasting brew that gives +10 to RRs against disease for 1-100 days. Melandar keeps well when it has been dried, and many healers have a small stock of it.

foragables.name: Melem Loza
foragables.characteristics: The small, dull green leaves of melem loza, its tiny, orange, spring blossoms, and its thick stem distinguish this vine from its neighbours.
foragables.medicinalUses: Sap from the melem loza stem is capable of halving the effects of any 1st or 2nd degree burn. It keeps its virtue for up to 2 days. A balm made from this sap doubles the effects of any healing magic. The art of its making is a closely guarded secret of the Kentriba Ladnoca of Tresti. The balm lasts nearly indefinitely.
foragables.cost: 60 gp/sap; 150 gp/dose of balm (because of the difficulty in recognizing the plant among the others in the region

foragables.name: Menelar
foragables.characteristics: This is a rare dwarf spruce of frigid coniferous forests, found most frequently near the timber line. It has dark blue-green needles which grow in clusters of five and long, tapering, dark brown cones.
foragables.medicinalUses: A tea brewed from the mature, but unopened cones creates a Level 7 antidote for circulatory poisons.

foragables.name: Merrig
foragables.characteristics: Merrig is a low bush distinguishable by the tightly wound spiral growth pattern. Its leaves are pear-shaped (dark green on top, light green on the bottom). Its woody stem is covered with small thorns.
foragables.medicinalUses: Merrig thorns may be scraped off and boiled overnight until a thick liquid remains (the thorns long having since dissolved). Daily ingestion increases Pr and Ap by 5. This effect occurs after 10 days of use.
foragables.warning:
Addiction to merrig occurs after 2 weeks.
Interruption and withdrawal from use means loss of stats (-10 Co, -5 Int, -5 Pr and -5 Ap)

foragables.name: Metsästäjän Kukka
foragables.characteristics: This light blue flower blooms close to the ground in thick clusters in the high valleys of Forochel’s mountains.
foragables.otherUses:
When ground and formed into a thick paste, metsästäjän kukka may be applied to the edge of a weapon or smeared into a drinking cup or food bowl. The Lossoth smear the poison on spears and arrows when hunting, seeing that it saves them from losing wounded seals and walruses who would otherwise take to the sea.
The poison is extremely virulent and kills instantly.
foragables.cost: he Lossoth do not value currency, but would barter metsästäjän kukka for needful items (e.g., blankets, pelts, dried fruit, etc).

foragables.name: Milkpurse
foragables.characteristics: This plant is remarkable for its plain, 3' stalk (square in cross section), and the white and yellow flowers that sprout from its top. Its short, pointed leaves have jagged edges and sprout from the nodes that occur every 6" along the stalk. Immediately above the nodes are swellings the size of plums. If cut open, a copious amount of white sap spills out. It is sticky and dries into a film within 1 hour.
foragables.medicinalUses: If rubbed 2x/day into the welts that cause the disease known as angurth, the milk from the nodes of this plant cause the redness to disappear over the next week. During this time, the disease does not progress and is in remission. If mixed with water and taken internally concurrently with application to the skin, the milk cures the disease over the period of 1 week.
foragables.otherUses: If cut and dried, the nodes become rattles and are a favourite of children in some villages.

foragables.name: Mirenna
foragables.characteristics: Mirgalen is a low-lying shrub with black, twisted branches, Its pale green leaves are perfectly round, sprouting in clusters of 3, The plant blooms early in spring, when snow is still deep on the ground; its berries emerge at the onset of summer. The tart, green berries must be picked within 1 week of maturation, falling to the ground and germinating soon after. The berries keep for 2 weeks before drying out and becoming useless.
foragables.medicinalUses: If quickly bitten and swallowed, a mirgalen berry instantly restores 10 hits. Some warriors fight with a berry wedged between their teeth and the side of the mouth, swallowing it in the event of a wound.

foragables.name: Míretári’s Crown
foragables.characteristics: Míretári’s Crown resembles a small lily, and remains in bloom for most of the short growing season. Its flowers are silky to the touch and have nearly no scent, If kept in water, picked flowers remain fresh for up to 1 week.
foragables.medicinalUses: If laid across an open wound, the flowers halt bleeding, turning blood-red as they adhere to the damaged flesh. Bleeding resumes unless the flowers are left in place for 10 minutes, after which they may be removed. The flowers cannot actually close a wound.
foragables.otherUses: Mountain folk often keep a vase of these pretty flowers, both to brighten the home and to provide some rudimentary first aid.

foragables.name: Monkmeg
foragables.characteristics: No more than 12' in height, this small tree has pointed, oval leaves, Sap from the tree is constantly leaking from small cracks in the bark and oozing down the trunk, Light brown, almond-shaped nuts (about 1" in length) appear in late summer.
foragables.medicinalUses: Monkmeg sap may be easily collected. If spread on a wart, the growth disappears within 2-3 days.
foragables.otherUses: The outer coating of the nuts may be grated to yield a tasty spice that is often added to sweet pies.

foragables.name: Monk Hair
foragables.characteristics: Monk hair is a light brown species of algae that grows in shallow water. It measures about 1' in length and is very fine, like a thick piece of hair. It usually grows in small patches no more than 2' in diameter.
foragables.medicinalUses: If dried and powdered, monk hair halts all bleeding — internal and external — in an injured person. The powdered algae does not close wounds.
foragables.otherUses: Powdered monk hair is an antidote for the poison karfar, but only if administered within a minute of the poison’s activation.

foragables.name: Mook
foragables.characteristics: This 30’ tall member of the juniper family resembles a thick shrub. Its thick, green leaves splinter into dozens of short tendrils. The berries, which appear in late summer, are grey and shaped like small crowned thimbles.
foragables.medicinalUses: The Danak first discovered that mook berries may be collected, ground and fermented to yield a dark brew. When distilled into an elixir, the berries become a level 8 antidote for all respiratory poisons. The antidote keeps for years.

foragables.name: Moonthumb
foragables.characteristics: This fungus (the size and shape of a man’s thumb) is curved backwards, like a toadstool without a head and requires total darkness to grow, preferably near running water. It emits a faint light and grows in patches of several dozen members.
foragables.medicinalUses: Eating moonthumb instantly restores 1-10 concussion hits. If dried, it loses its luminosity, but retains its healing virtue.

foragables.name: Morhereg
foragables.characteristics: A small blue flower that grows deep in old-growth forests. It stands about 6" tall and has several short, greenish-black leaves,
foragables.otherUses:
If ground, made into a paste and applied to a weapon, morhereg becomes a Ist level blood poison. Its victim's veins temporarily run with kalirion, a black liquid that serves as imperfect blood, sustaining life, but incapacitating.
Temporary mental stats (Em, In, Me, Pr, Re) fall by 50 but do not sink below I. The black-skinned victim returns to normal after 1-10 hours, but stats recuperate at rate of only 1/day. Some slave traders favour morhereg as a means of subduing their victims.

foragables.name: Mothernel
foragables.characteristics: This small, parasitic plant, reminiscent of a mistletoe, is found tapping into the trunk at the top of evergreen trees, using their sap as a source of nutrition to supplement its photosynthesis.
foragables.medicinalUses: If ground, mixed with water and ingested, mothernel leaves protect the consumer from the effects of all poisons for 1 hour. If administered after someone has been poisoned, however, it is only effective as an antidote for jegga.
foragables.warning: Anyone consuming this drug finds that their urine turns the colour of blood for 24 hours. If they are not aware that this effect is natural and unharmful, considerable mental anguish could result as they imagine themselves poisoned in spite of the protection,

foragables.name: Mountainrod
foragables.characteristics: Mountainrod is a member of the reed family and is found near a source of water. It grows to a height of about S' and is usually found in thick clumps. The stalk is light brown and the thick tip, dark brown, Its long, green leaves are pointed, peeling off from the stalk as it rises.
foragables.medicinalUses: If crushed and boiled for 10 minutes, the mountainrod stalk produces a bitter tea that hastens the healing of broken bones (5x normal rate) for a period of 2 days.
foragables.warning: If not properly set when the brew is drunk, the bones may heal improperly, permanently impairing the patient.

foragables.name: Mountainthorn
foragables.characteristics: This vine prefers to live on rock faces, especially those with a high moisture content (such as near waterfalls), It can reach lengths of 30’ and its hold on the rock is astounding, Deceptively thin, its light green stem can easily support a man’s weight. Its triangular leaves are spaced out so they average about 1 every foot.
foragables.medicinalUses: If thrown into a fire until it blackens, and then crushed, the powdered mountainthorn stem eases breathing, making it more efficient and enabling the inhaler to exert himself for 2x the normal amount of time before becoming winded.
foragables.otherUses: Mountainthorn is sometimes used to treat the disease bukandas.

foragables.name: Mountainweed
foragables.characteristics: This herb has several stalks, all ending in large leaves the size and shape of a man’s foot. It boasts a single, small flower sprout in the centre at ground level, blue like the sky on a clear, early summer day
foragables.medicinalUses: If dried and crushed, the powdered mountainweed secretes a substance from the ingester’s palms which, while remaining barely noticeable to the eye (like a thin sheen of sweat), causes anything coming in contact with it to adhere with enough force that it must be forcibly pried from the hands, The secretion takes 10 minutes to take effect and wears off after 1 hour.

foragables.name: Muilfana
foragables.characteristics: This is a pine tree native to cool, temperate coniferous forests with acidic soils.
foragables.otherUses: The sap is concentrated to create an orange liquid that reacts with certain enzymes present in mucus, producing a powerful acid which destroys mucous membrane tissue.Target organs included the eyes, the respiratory system (particularly the windpipe or trachea), the digestive system (particularly the oesophagus), the urinary tract, and the genitalia.

foragables.name: Mur
foragables.characteristics: This low shrub (which grows to a height of about 2") resembles its relatives, boswillia and myrrh, Its greyish-brown bark is covered with thin, white stripes running up and down. In the spring, red berries come out.
foragables.medicinalUses: If mur bark is scored, its resin may be collected. Through a process known only to a few healers (which involves boiling, baking and stirring before mixing with blood), mur may become a lifekeeping infusion. The resin may be kept for up to 6 months, but the concoction maintains potency for only a few hours.

foragables.name: Mustakuu
foragables.characteristics: Mustakuu is a black, globular fungus.
foragables.otherUses: The residue of oil gleaned by skimming the surface of the water in which mustakuu is boiled attracts the insatiable insect swarms of the Far North, driving them into a frenzy and drawing them irresistibly to anything smeared with it. In the spring and summer seasons, when the swarms are thick and troublesome, the Lossothrin hunters carry tightly-sealed bone tubes of the oil. When they bed down for the evening, they drip a little of it on rocks and plants surrounding their camp, thus drawing the insects away from their repose.
foragables.warning: The oil attracts insects for up to 8 hours and is difficult to wash off. Victims can die of severe anaemia after a few hours of being in the eye of a swarm.
foragables.cost: The Lossoth are happy to barter mustakuu for other goods which they need.

foragables.name: Näkökasvi
foragables.characteristics: Nakikasvi is a small, greyish, thistle-like plant with yellow roots.
foragables.medicinalUses: hen brewed into a liquid form, näkökasvi roots help to restore sight (much as a Major Eye Repair spell), especially for those afflicted by snow-blindness. The root-concoction may either be imbibed or applied directly as a wet poultice to the injured eye. If imbibed, sight is restored in 12-24 hours, 1-8 hours in poultice form.
foragables.cost: The Lossoth are happy to barter näkökasvi roots for other goods which they need.

foragables.name: Nashadt
foragables.characteristics: This succulent plant grows to a height of 1' and has several thick, rubbery stalks with dozens of leaves along them. The leaves (also thick and rubbery) are oval-shaped with pointed ends.
foragables.medicinalUses: If crushed and placed in hot (but not boiling) water, nashadt leaves yield a sweet-tasting tea that warms the imbiber all over. If suffering from hypothermia, the imbiber is restored to normal body temperature in a matter of minutes. The sudden influx of heat, however, makes him drowsy, demanding at least 1 hour of sleep.
foragables.otherUses: The tea is also useful as an antidote for the poison urána.

foragables.name: Nehtelassë
foragables.characteristics: This small bush grows to a height of about 3'. It has silvery bark, reddish thorns and finger-shaped, silvery leaves.
foragables.medicinalUses: The silver-green leaves are rubbed on the skin to relieve small bumps and bruises, restoring 1-6 concussion hits.

foragables.name: Nelisse
foragables.characteristics: This bush is distantly related to coca, with small ovalate leaves.
foragables.medicinalUses: The leaves are brewed into a tea, which when ingested causes euphoria for 1 hour (all action -50) and yields 1 day's nutrition.
foragables.warning: Use of the tea more than twice in a one week, or 5 times in a month can cause addiction, with the victim suffering severe headaches for 1-3 months and all mental temporary stats dropping by 5 for this period.

foragables.name: Nelluin
foragables.characteristics: Nelluin is a lichen that grows low on the southern side of spruce trees. It is distinguished by its dark blue colour and rough texture.
foragables.medicinalUses: Nelluin may be boiled and strained to yield a tea of incredible healing virtue. Drinking 1 cup of this tea heals any nerve damage the consumer has sustained.
foragables.warning: Drinking nelluin tea permanently stains the teeth a light blue.

foragables.name: Nelthandon
foragables.characteristics: Nelthandon resembles those types of plants typically used for wild salad greens. It is unremarkable in its appearance, looking much like a dandelion (even to the point of producing an orange-yellow flower). Unlike the dandelion, however, nelthandon’s flower won't turn grey and blow away; instead, it simply withers at the end of the spring. Another difference between nelthandon and dandelion is that the former has a yellow vein on the bottom of each leaf.
foragables.medicinalUses: If someone has ingested poison, a small piece of this plant induces immediate and powerful vomiting.
foragables.otherUses: Sometimes young Hillmen serve strangers a salad of “wild greens” and sit back to watch the fun
foragables.warning:
Travellers in strange lands and distrustful of the locals should avoid eating a salad of “wild greens”. On the other hand, if trust is required before the locals deal with
travellers, and the locals know the travellers know about nelthandon, eating a suspicious but harmless salad can go a long way toward establishing relations.

foragables.name: Nightfoot
foragables.characteristics: his plant resembles a dead jack-in-the-pulpit: the hood of the flower is sunken, curled up, the whole flower appears ready to fall off. At night, however, it rears up proudly and the flower unfurls a huge, magnificent blossom.
foragables.medicinalUses: If picked at night and crushed before being eaten, nightfoot confers the ability to see in total darkness as though it were dusk (1 hour duration). The flower is only good until dawn; when the rays of the sun strike it, the blossom shrivels and lose its virtue.
foragables.otherUses: Consuming a night-picked flower is one of two antidotes known for the poison zaganzar.

foragables.name: Nightrod
foragables.characteristics: his small mushroom is easily distinguished by its black colour and shiny surface. It grows like a toadstool, but its cap is elongated and pointed like a cone. It is normally found in clumps numbering up to a dozen on or bear organic matter. Nightrod grows to about the height and girth of a man’s index finger.
foragables.medicinalUses: If consumed, a nightrod cap restores 1-2 hits. Kept fresh (e.g., in a sealed jar), its potency remains for several months; once dry, it is worthless.
foragables.otherUses: Dried and smoked, nightrod is a tasty addition to any salad. Dwarves make a secret soup from this fungus rarely served to outsiders and reputed to be beyond description in taste.

foragables.name: Nimgil
foragables.characteristics:
This white flower only grows a few inches in height (its blossom about the size of a man’s thumbnail). Its interior is thick with stamen and pistils, If squeezed, nimgil yields a few drops of nectar. The plant blooms all year round; its flowers grow in groups of 3/plant.

It is eagerly sought after, so any plants within easy reach are picked and long gone by the time travellers seek them. Reaching the flower is usually a difficult act to get it from the mountain-cliffs where it grows.
foragables.medicinalUses: A drop of mimgil nectar invigorates its imbiber, restoring I-10 hits and giving him +S to all actions for the next 24 hours, The nectar loses its power within minutes of being harvested.
foragables.warning: Nimgil’s effect works only once/person/24 hour period. However, the imbiber may think the effect is cumulative, which can lead to errors in judgement.

foragables.name: Nimnaur
foragables.characteristics: The whitefiddle spider is a species of "lesser great" spider named for the distinctive white mark on its back.
foragables.otherUses: The milky white venom of the spider can be concentrated to produce nimnaur poison that slowly liquefies one organ over 1-10 minutes, usually the one closest to the entry point.

foragables.name: Nur-oiolosse
foragables.characteristics: This is an enchanted clove that grows in the harsh north.
foragables.medicinalUses: Eating a clove provides Lifegiving for 1 day for all races, however it kills 1 day later unless a Sorel nut is ingested.

foragables.name: Oiolossë
foragables.characteristics: This herb’s bulbous root sends up a simple stem 1-5' in height. Its long, taper-pointed leaves (1-2' in length, 1-2" wide) are white veined and toothed along their edges. During the short growing season, oiolossë can grow up to 1"/ day. Tiny, yellow flowers sprout from the stem in midsummer. If dug up, the oiolossë root can easily be separated into several dozen cloves, like a monster head of garlic.
foragables.medicinalUses: An EIf who consumes an oiolossë clove enjoys protection from any harm or degeneration, no matter how grievous his wounds or injury. This effect lasts for 2 days, during which time all healing herbs and magics work at maximum potency.

foragables.name: Olvar
foragables.characteristics: Olvar is a small low-lying shrub rarely reaching over 6" in height. It is to be found in the shores of saltwaters coasts in the spray zone. The flowers are pale blue star shaped with narrow petals.
foragables.medicinalUses: If the flower is ingested it will preserve a body for between 2-20 days, essentially stopping the clock on the subjects injuries.

foragables.name: Olvatári
foragables.characteristics: Olvatári is a short shrub with shiny, round leaves and 1" long thorns. A rare plant, it bears fruit and silver-white flowers for a very short time in summer.
foragables.medicinalUses: The juice from an olvatári fruit heals all burns, regardless of their severity, restores 1-10 hits and eliminates scar tissue. The juice keeps for up to 2 years.

foragables.name: Ondohithui
foragables.characteristics: This is a blue-grey lichen found most frequently growing between the highest peak rocks.
foragables.otherUses: A paste is prepared by carefully collecting, washing, and grinding the lichen into powder, then mixing the powder with lard.

foragables.name: Ondokamba
foragables.characteristics: The Ondokamba bat is unusual in that it like cold climes, living in the caves and caverns of northern mountains and hills.
foragables.otherUses: If the saliva of the bat is harvested and condensed a green venom can be made that turns extremeties to stone. Uncondensed it is also poisonous but only causes a mild, temporary loss of dexterity in the hands and/or feet.

foragables.name: Other Eyes
foragables.characteristics: This mushroom appears as a slimy, many capped mass. Each cap boasts a single patch of red pigment that resembles an eye. Each cap is 1' in diameter.
foragables.otherUses: When eaten, the flesh of the mushroom confers the ability to see hidden things for 2 hours. Other eyes are only effective when the fungi are freshly picked.
foragables.warning: The effect may be repeated 2x before the eater becomes immune to it and must wait for 1 week for his body to shake off the effects of the drug before resuming consumption.

foragables.name: Pangwood
foragables.characteristics: This low-growing shrubby tree often forms dense thickets on islets and along channels. Its twigs and pointed, arrow-head shaped leaves are covered with fine, short, seemingly downy hairs that are, in reality, sharp enough to pierce the skin of most peoples (though Orcs have some resistance because of the their tough hides).
foragables.otherUses:
When ingested, pangwood sap immunises against all poisons (except its own hairs) for 72 hours.

Numerous trips are requited to harvest a single dose.

foragables.name: Pargen
foragables.characteristics: This lush bush with a brown, segmented stem possesses long, pointed leaves and looks like just another member of the palm family. On the underside of its uppermost fan of leaves is a cluster of dark red berries.
foragables.medicinalUses: An invalid who ingests a handful of pargen berries experiences no deterioration in their condition for 4 days. During this time, all healing magics and herbs work at maximum potency. Pargen berries keep for several months.

foragables.name: Pasámar
foragables.characteristics: A short, fine, dark green grass, related to Sîriëna, Pasámar is native to tropical grasslands or savannas, growing in tight clumps.
foragables.medicinalUses: When properly cleaned and brewed, pasámar broth preserves organic material (up to body size) indefinitely.
foragables.warning: If ingested, this broth is a very strong (level 8) reduction poison which attacks the gastrointestinal system.

foragables.name: Pathúr
foragables.characteristics: A small enchanted shrub related to the sage, pathúr is native to arid scrublands.
foragables.medicinalUses: When rubbed on the patient's chest, a broth brewed from its water-storing root nodules was Lifekeeping for one hour.
foragables.warning: If ingested, this broth is a mid-strong (level 5) nerve poison.

foragables.name: Pepperglove
foragables.characteristics: This small orchid grows in the forks of branches set high in the trees of tropical forests. It has 1 large leaf with 5 lobes. It also produces small, black berries and a white flower with black spots (also 5 lobed).
foragables.medicinalUses: Ingesting pepperglove berries bestows incredible peace of mind, restoring 1-10 hits as the subject falls into a restful slumber that lasts 4-8 hours. The subject awakens refreshed, no matter how fatigued he was before.
foragables.otherUses: When combined with kingsfoot, pepperglove berries cure the disease grelnixar.

foragables.name: Perimound
foragables.characteristics: This small herb grows no more than a few inches in height and is distinguishable by its numerous, oval-shaped leaves sprouting all along the stalk, which splits into several branches at the tip, where dozens of minute orange flowers blossom in summer.
foragables.medicinalUses: When crushed and consumed, perimound flowers cause the ingester’s bones to become weak and brittle, like chalk, for a period of 24 hours. Afterwards they harden to their previous state over the space of 2 days. Healers use this drug to weaken any bones that have been poorly set, enabling them to re-set them properly so that healing may occur.
foragables.warning: Because of the danger of being injured, someone under the influence of this drug should take care to avoid any sudden, jarring movements. It is also rumoured that the drug has been used as an insidious poison to set someone up for an “accidental” tumble down a set of stairs, an incident that would probably prove fatal.

foragables.name: Phacalus
foragables.characteristics: This member of the reed family differs from its relatives in that it has a tuberous root the size of a man’s thumb and because it rarely reaches a height of greater than 3'. Consequently, it is often hard to find.
foragables.medicinalUses: If dried and ground, the pharalus root may be applied to a wound to prevent bleeding within 5 minutes. It does not close the wound, The root must be dried for at least 1 week in the sun to become effective.
foragables.otherUses: The phacalus root is used by the Beffraen in their ceremonies. Swallowed whole, the root permanently increases the user's Presence, Reasoning, Intuition, Empathy and Memory by 1 point each (not to exceed 102). However, with each dose there is a chance that the user may have one of two negative reactions to the herb (35% of a reaction with a 50-50 chance of either type occurring).
foragables.warning:
Two negative reactions to the phacalus root are possible.
  • The first (completely independent of the quantity of herb ingested) is severe and immediate: the subject falls into a coma, awakening 4 days later much the weaker (stats previously increased by the root are now reduced by 15 points). Up to half of these lost points (round up) may be regained through magic and healing, but no more than half.
  • The second negative reaction is allergic and come in several forms, from mild to deadly. In all such cases there is no stat increase (RR vs 17th level poison).
    • If the RR is successful, the subject receives only a minor rash.
    • 1-24: multiple blisters form on his elbows, knees and groin, causing immobilization for at least 10 days;
    • 25-49: the subject goes into immediate anaphylactic shock, dying within 30 minutes if not treated (If he survives, 2 months of debilitation follows.);
    • 50+: the subject's skin sloughs off completely over the next 1-4 days, dying in terrible pain with nothing left but bare muscles and bone. In this last scenario, the victim’s only hope are the spells Lifekeeping or Lifegiving (The body starts to respond after 15 days of such treatment.)
Not all the effects of phacalus are known to most of its users, and the root has been responsible for many deaths.

foragables.name: Pigmint
foragables.characteristics: This herb grows to a height of 4', sprouting numerous branches along the length of its stalk. Each branch splits into several more, and each of these has several, small, pointed, oval-shaped leaves with serrated edges. If crushed, the leaves smell strongly of mint. It is often cultivated in gardens.
foragables.medicinalUses: Anyone eating the leaves from this plant experiences a chill. A tea made from the leaves causes shivering as though submerged in ice water. Healers use this tea to reduce and break fevers.
foragables.otherUses:
Farmers who raise swine often cultivate this plant as a treat for their livestock (who seem to love its taste, but are immune to its effects). In addition, pigmint tea can
rouse someone from a coma brought on by the poison klytun

foragables.name: Plant-like Stone
foragables.characteristics: This fungus grows very close to the ground and resembles loose stones.
foragables.medicinalUses: The fungus contains milky white sap (a carefully guarded secret known only to Dwarves) which, when squeezed directly onto open wounds, halts bleeding, sealing the wound as the liquid dries and preventing infection.
foragables.warning: Since Dwarves consider this fungus a cultural secret, a good way to quickly anger a Dwarf 1s to make a joke about “getting blood from a stone”.

foragables.name: Poison Willow
foragables.characteristics: Poison willow closely resembles the weeping willow, except that it only reaches a height of 25'. Its shiny, yellow-green leaves are edged with a thin strip of orange-coloured tissue.
foragables.warning: Any skin contact with the willow’s oily leaves causes painful blisters 1 hour later. The inflammation lasts for 1 week, and may be healed by a poultice of ironleaf.

foragables.name: Primhock
foragables.characteristics: This bush is composed of several stalks, each straight and divided into 6" segments joined by knuckle-like joints. The leaves (2" long, ½" wide) sprout straight from the stalk. It grows at the edges of deciduous forests and grasslands.
foragables.otherUses: If chewed for 10 minutes, a primhock leaf causes water retention for a period of 72 hours. During this time the consumer cannot sweat or salivate, and his urine becomes so concentrated as to actually appear dark yellow. On the other hand, he becomes capable of resisting dehydration quite effectively (e.g., while traversing a desert).
foragables.warning: Anyone taking 2 consecutive doses of primhock without a day of total rehydration irrevocably damages his kidneys, dying 1 week later from renal failure.

foragables.name: Puff Spice
foragables.characteristics: This fungus is a type of mushroom, distinctive because it has no stalk. Its round cap (light brown with tiny, black spots) grows directly on whatever substrate it is feeding upon, usually rotting wood. If squeezed, it emits a puff of spores.
foragables.otherUses: If an intact (un-squeezed) puff-spice fungus is slowly crushed, it may be mixed with nelluin to serve as antidote for the poison dynallea.
foragables.warning: 12 hours after ingesting this fungus, all hair on the subject’s body falls out. It take a few weeks to grow back.

foragables.name: Queenstaff
foragables.characteristics: This small but sturdy tree grows only to a height of 5', producing leaves from its uppermost branches. Its smooth bark is green-grey. In late summer, queenstaff produces purple, egg-sized fruits that have a tart taste, but are otherwise edible, Queenstaff is a rare species that takes hundreds of years to mature
foragables.medicinalUses: If 1' square of queenstaff bark is stripped, boiled and imbibed, it heals any brain damage over the next 12 hours.
foragables.otherUses: The entire tree is sometimes stripped of its bark and branches and used as a walking stick. However, healers who live near the wetlands discourage this because of its rarity.

foragables.name: Quilmufûr
foragables.characteristics: Quilmufûr is a rare floor plant of temperate coniferous forests, found most frequently near clearings or aspen groves.It had dark green leaves with five leaflets, a large night-blooming white flower, and a cluster of white berries.
foragables.medicinalUses: A tea brewed from its roots contains a level 8 antidote for conversion poisons.
foragables.warning: If ingested, the leaves, flowers, and fruit contain a mild level 3 reduction poison which attacks the gastrointestinal system.

foragables.name: Rabbit Thumb
foragables.characteristics: This fuzzy, light brown fungus grows to the size of a raisin in patches that quickly spread, entirely covering the droppings on which they thrive
foragables.medicinalUses: When brewed with true tarnas, rabbit thumb has the power to cure the disease igturfas.

foragables.name: Red Willow
foragables.characteristics: The leaves of this small willow at first show the normal silvery green of the common willow, but by early summer they begin a slow transformation, first becoming a silvery rose and then, by autumn, a brilliant scarlet
foragables.medicinalUses:
The extract of red willow leaves, when heated and distilled, is an excellent cure for fever, and this is one of the most important weapons in the never-ending war against the many fever-producing illnesses prevalent in wetlands, When brewed in combination with it, red willow extract doubles the potency of the common healing herb tburl, and also relieves pain and swelling.

In extract form, red willow may be mixed with any good wine, sealed against air and stored almost indefinitely. 1-10 oz of the resulting scarlet potion (often called red gift or marsh wine) may be imbibed within a given day; larger dosages result in nausea, falling blood pressure and eventual coma.
foragables.otherUses: Red willow leaves are also used in preparation of the healing salve “cooling foam,” a balm made by grinding the leaves, mixing them with an oily base and allowing this to sit for about a year.
foragables.cost: 3 sp/leaf; 33 gp/dose (1 oz) of red gift

foragables.name: Reglen
foragables.characteristics: This moss is unremarkable, being dark green and short, except that the underside is reddish when peeled up.
foragables.medicinalUses: Reglen is dried and brewed into a healing draught. One of the best of the “simple” curatives, its damage restoration calms the patient and allows natural healing to begin, Reglen restores 5-50 hits, and retains its potency for up to a month.
foragables.otherUses: Moss

foragables.name: Rewk
foragables.characteristics: This woody shrub prefers the darkness of a deep forest, often extending its branches over a quietly burbling stream, and growing to several feet in height and width. Rewk leaves (nearly 1' long, growing in groups of 5) are light green on top, pink underneath and teardrop-shaped. If the roots at the base of the plant are exposed, several soft, brown nodules the size of peas are found on their outlying ends,
foragables.medicinalUses: A handful of rewk nodules may be washed, cut in half and boiled for 1 hour to produce a brew that instantly restores 2-20 hits
foragables.otherUses: Nodule

foragables.name: Rigána
foragables.characteristics: This vine has pointed leaves that grow in clusters of 3 (often variegated with a bright crimson). The surface of the leaves is thinly coated with an oil.
foragables.warning: The oil of rigana leaves causes an itchy rash from even the slightest contact. The rash lasts for 4-7 days, distracting the victim's every activity.

foragables.name: Rolling Reed
foragables.characteristics: his member of the reed family distinguishes itself from its cousins by the fact chat, as it ages, its light brown stalk begins to curve back toward the ground until, by the time it dies, its dark brown head begins to point upward again, thus nearly completing a full circle.
foragables.medicinalUses: If dried and ground, the root of the rolling reed may be mixed with water; when consumed, the mixture slows the imbiber’s metabolism, enabling him to hold his breath for 6 minutes. The subject must then breath normally for 1 hour before being able to repeat this feat. The effect lasts for 1 hour.
foragables.otherUses: Rolling reeds are often dried and used as children’s toys, or as decorations in villages located near to where it grows.

foragables.name: Rosecreeper
foragables.characteristics: This vine prefers to grow near roses or other similar bushes, entwining itself into their branches, It has a dark, brown-green stem and leaves that match those of a rose. (Its thorns, however, are much longer.) Its flowers also resemble those of a rose, but are sickly, yellow-green in hue (which leads gardeners to strive to keep the creepers out of their gardens). Once thoroughly entwined in a bush, rosecreepers are nearly impossible to get rid of without a great deal of effort and a great number of scratches.
foragables.medicinalUses: Dried and powdered, the rosecreeper flower ylelds an effective antidote for the poison taynaga.

foragables.name: Rose Tree
foragables.characteristics:
These shrubs grow dense and tall, like a hedge of lilacs, and their beautiful flowers of pure white and burgundy cluster together over nearly every inch of these trees as they bloom. Rose tree flowers hide their parent's bite, however, because they are covered with needle-sharp thorns during the blooming months (Lothron through Iyanneth). Only wild goats are impervious to the thorns (being capable of eating through nearly anything).

These trees were planted by Elves long ago in an effort co mark their boundaries of their realms.
foragables.otherUses: The extracted nectar of these trees (called mirvellen) holds great virtue for enchantments (+25 to spells on objects so covered), and Elven healers frequently use this power to aid their magics for cleansing the body of poison.

foragables.name: Rud-tekma
foragables.characteristics: This tree grows to a height of about 40' and is famous for its gnarled, twisted, black bark. Its red leaves are hand-shaped. For most of the year, the tree bears reddish, tart, pear-like fruit.
foragables.otherUses:
If eaten by a magician, red temka fruit enhances his ability to cast essence spells for 1 hour:
  • -20 manoeuvre and melee.
  • +20 to spells attacks.
  • 10% chance target spell will hit nearest target rather than intended

The fruit is only effective while fresh (keeping about 1 week after being picked)
foragables.warning: After eating a rud-temka fruit, the consumer finds his movement and melee negatively affected for the next hour. Eating more than 3 fruits/week or 10 fruits/month causes addiction, resulting in loss of all PPs for 1-6 months if the subject attempts to quit.

foragables.name: Rúthin
foragables.characteristics: Rúthin is a series of crystals that grow up to 3" tall in an exotic, plant-like shape,
foragables.otherUses: This rock crystal, found in caves in the Trollshaws, is prepared with herbs as a liquid suspension. Used as an ingested poison, an RR failure turns the contents of the victim's stomach into jagged shards of glass, causing death in 6-12 rounds. (There is no effect if the victim has not eaten within the last 6 hours.)
foragables.warning: There is no antidote for this poison

foragables.name: Ruth-i-laur
foragables.characteristics: A brownish liquid which can be refined from the saliva of most species of drakes and their relatives, usually by extracting the saliva with vegetable oils.
foragables.otherUses: The extracted saliva is distilled to produce ruth-i-laur, a level 4 nerve poison causing rapid (1-20 rounds) erosion of the nervous system, leaving the victim at -50 to -100 activity (-50 for RR failures of 1-25, -75 for failures of 26-50, or -100 for failures of 51 or more).

foragables.name: Saewedhil
foragables.characteristics: This small bush has perfectly straight stems, which rise in every direction out of a central cluster, peppered with small, round leaves and thick, short thorns. Resistant to drought, saewedhil always looks as if it has gone a month without water, After its first season, (during which time it is green and lush), saewedhil appears to dry out, but still sports small, white flowers every other year.
foragables.otherUses:
If gathered and ground into a powder, saewedhil leaves make an devastating poison. Usually administered orally, it takes effect within seconds with deadly accuracy:
Elves are killed instantly; all others are placed in a coma for 2-6 weeks.
foragables.warning:
The main barrier to finding an antidote to saewedhil is the fact that the victim (if Elven) is dead so quickly that there isn’t time to fetch one. It is rumoured that a tea made of ladylock neutralises the poison; however, drinking this tea before eating food tainted with saewedhil does not stay the toxin (since the body alters tea almost immediately upon ingestion). If any traces of saewedhil are present, however, the tea attaches itself to them, tracking the poison’s progress though the body.

Being a powder, the saewedhil toxin cannot be mixed with water or smeared on a blade. If water or any other liquid is added, its deadly power fades rapidly after about 1 minute's time.

Any who prepare saewedhil or come in contact with it should take care to clean their hands well before sitting down to eat anything. The poison gives off the scent of roasted mushrooms. If a victim is aware of this, he may perceive that something is amiss.

foragables.name: Sailchas
foragables.characteristics: This small, violet orchid blooms throughout the spring, being a quiet, light greenish-brown the rest of the year. The plant rarely gets larger than 8" in diameter.
foragables.otherUses: The Eriadorians believe sailchas blossoms to be a potent harbinger of good luck, Until the bloom withers (3-7 days from picking), sailchas confers +10 morale, +10 to RRs and +S DB upon its wearer.

foragables.name: Sandclaw
foragables.characteristics: This twisted bush grows to a height of 5', its gnarled, brown branches disguised by thousands of thin, elongated leaves the size of a man’s finger. Each leaf is rounded at its tip, green on top and grey underneath. It prefers rocky beaches to sand.
foragables.medicinalUses: When crushed and packed into an asp-envenomed blade wound, sandclaw leaves neutralise any of the toxin that hasn’t yet acted on its victim. The leaves are effective whether fresh or dried, and keep for years in the latter state.
foragables.warning: Sandclaw leaves do not close a wound or stop bleeding, nor can they be effectively applied after the wound has been staunched and sealed.

foragables.name: Scrumpy
foragables.characteristics: A beverage made from honey and various fermented swamp plants native to Ethir Anduin, scrumpy has the colour and consistency of good stout; its taste and alcohol content vary according to quality. The hallucinogenic and addictive qualities of scrumpy derive from a secret ingredient: the poisonous blood of the Ethir swamp-dragon (a species of crocodile).
foragables.otherUses:
The effects of scrumpy upon a “virgin imbiber” are unpredictable, requiring an RR vs Ist level poison:
  • 0-15: paranoid hysteria
  • 16-25: hallucinations
  • 26-75: vomiting
  • 76-85: seizures
  • 86-00: death
Initial effects wear off in 4-6 hours, although a devastating hangover is normal for 8-12 hours.

For those who dare to come back for a second try, scrumpy produces pleasant intoxication, along with a welcome shot of courage and inspiration without unpleasant side effects. Excessive consumption at any one time produces hallucinations, feelings of euphoria (or paranoia) and, occasionally, delusions of grandeur which may inspire rash or foolhardy behaviour

Experienced scrumpoholics can generally control these symptoms, but true addicts become subject to obsessive behaviour and unpredictable mood swings. Each successive draught reduces the consumer's RR to such effects by 1.
foragables.warning: Scrumpy tends to be publicly scorned by the Dúnedain nobility of Gondor and Umbar, who associate the drink with pirates and criminal lowlife. It is, however, secretly enjoyed by many of their number, a fact which helps to keep the illicit trade alive.

foragables.name: Seathorn
foragables.characteristics: This brown floating plant resembles nothing so much as a tangled ball of extremely sharp thorns (which can reach 1" in length). Upon closer examination, however, tiny brown leaves become visible, blending with the tangled knot of the stem, along which several nodules cling, housing the plant's fruit. The nodules (often referred to as “barnacles”) are white on the outside with a small brown hole at the top.
foragables.medicinalUses: A seathorn barnacle restores 1-6 hits if consumed. Because of its tough coating, it keeps for several months before eventually drying up.
foragables.warning: Like a nut, the seathorn barnacle must be broken open if its meat is to be consumed. (Consuming one whole has no effect.) Anyone fool enough to pick up a seathorn tangle suffers I hit from being pricked. Merchants familiar with the plant collect the tangles with a forked stick.

foragables.name: Sha
foragables.characteristics: A member of the water lily family, sha has the characteristic flat, green, upper part that is visible above the surface of the water. Below the water hang dozens of roots. A single, pink blossom in the centre of the floating plant appears in spring.
foragables.otherUses: When dried, powdered and imbibed with any beverage, the sha flower confers the ability to see in all but total darkness (up to 300") for 1-5 rounds.
foragables.warning: 11-20 hours after consumption, the sha imbiber is stricken with severe diarrhoea for 1-5 days, reducing him (at best) to an ineffective state (-25) until he recovers.

foragables.name: Shadowvine
foragables.characteristics:
This creeper resembles a vine by its long stem and the sparsely-spaced leaves along its length. It differs primarily in that, in its mature form, it lacks a root, meandering along its course without beginning or end.

It is found within the entrance of caverns where dim light is available. It is also rumoured to be found in the deepest, darkest part of some forests or jungles, It cannot grow in light stronger than dim illumination. The vine prefers to adhere to stone surfaces.
foragables.medicinalUses: When pressed, shadowvine leaves yield an oil that is effective as an antidote for the poison jitsu. Pressed leaves keep indefinitely,

foragables.name: Shagu-Bitter
foragables.characteristics: This pale green mushroom usually has a cap 6" in diameter on a I' stalk. It tends to grow as a solitary individual.
foragables.otherUses: When scraped out, placed overnight in water and then slowly heated and reduced to a thick paste, the gills from this fungus yield an extremely toxic paralytic poison, which Orcish trackers sometimes place on their weapons. The bitter flesh of the mushroom has the same effect, but is impossible to apply to a blade.
foragables.warning: The only known antidote to shagu-bitter is a tea made from slimy gorkin. If the victim survives, the toxin wears off in 48 hours.

foragables.name: Sharag
foragables.characteristics: This small flower is only a few inches high. Its single blossom is pink; its leaves, short, pear-shaped and pointed.
foragables.medicinalUses: Small doses of powdered sharag blossom work to counteract the toxin slird, restoring its victim to normal health after 2 days of bed rest. Too much sharag can have fatal results. The very delicate task of administering the proper dosage is best left to an experienced healer.
foragables.otherUses: As a poison, sharag may be administered through food or drink—not at sword-point. Taking effect within I minute, its victim feels his extremities go limp, one by one, until his lungs and finally his heart stops over the space of the next minute. A very carefully measured dose of slird may be used as an antidote.
foragables.warning: Anyone working with this toxin should take care to wash their hands before eating, lest they wind up a victim

foragables.name: Shardúvâk
foragables.characteristics: This is a rare desert juniper with bright red berries.
foragables.otherUses: A bright brown juice may bve pressed from the berries which slows blood flow causing the victim to need double usual sleep until fully recovered. These effects could last several weeks or months.

foragables.name: Sharkásar
foragables.characteristics: This is a floor plant of temperate coniferous forests, found most frequently near clearings or aspen groves.It had dark green splayed leaves, a 1" purple and white flower, and a single white fruit.
foragables.otherUses: The root of the plant may be crushed and mixed with oil to form a brown paste that acts as a circulatory poison.

foragables.name: Sheep's Plume
foragables.characteristics: This member of the reed family is easily distinguished by the long, hairy fan at the top of its stalk. Its streamers reach lengths of up to 3.' (The entire plant can rise to a height of 6.") In fall, the streamers sail off on the wind, each bearing a seed.
foragables.medicinalUses: Boiling the frilly top of sheep's plume and straining the brew yields a tea that restores 2-20 concussion hits.
foragables.otherUses: Sheep's plume tea is also said to be good for curing the disease jadaras,

foragables.name: Shen
foragables.characteristics: This is an ivy with  dark green, three-fingered leaves.
foragables.otherUses: Level 4 antidote for Nerve Poison

foragables.name: Shimmer Sprig
foragables.characteristics: A lovely, shiny, green moss that grows in patches about the size and shape of a man’s leg. It appears to shimmer in the setting sun.
foragables.otherUses:
Eating this moss gives the ingester visions of natural activity in the surrounding area. It allows him to pick out non-natural activity by default, There is a chance that the sprig-chewer becomes overwhelmed by the wonders of nature, the most severe of the effects possible being a state of continual distraction due to flying birds, stinging gnats, attacking wolves and so on, Rangers and Wood-elves sometimes convince uninitiated comrades to “chew sprig” as a practical joke.

The range for the visions is 1 mile/level of the user. Observing non-natural activity is a Medium Perception manoeuver, An RR must be made each round the sprigs are chewed: if the chewer fails (1% chance failure/round used), he is overwhelmed, falling into a drooling stupor for 1 round/10% of failure, and forgetting 70% of what he has seen. If he fails by +51 or more, the chewer additionally undergoes a quasi-religious experience.

foragables.name: Silmaana
foragables.characteristics: Silmána is a tall plant, growing to 5' in height. It has several segmented stalks with small, diamond-shaped leaves at the nodes where these segments join. It flowers bright yellow in summer at its crest; 2 weeks later, dozens of small, black seeds fall to the ground.
foragables.otherUses:
When dried and ground into powder, silmána stalks become a potent poison that must be orally ingested to have effect. Its victim may detect the poison’s bitter taste, but that is their only warning before they receive 2-20 hits.

When mixed with oil and heated slowly for several hours, silmána powder scars any skin it comes in contact with (1-4 hits each), raising large blisters that heal slowly. If an open stag's purse is placed on the burn and changed every hour, it reduces the blisters, preventing scarification if repeated for 4 hours.

It is used by a number of cultures for personal decoration (scarification) or identification of slaves.

foragables.name: Silver Fir
foragables.characteristics: This evergreen often grows in small clumps and rarely reaches a height of more than 40', Its silver-green needles have blunt tips,
foragables.otherUses: If an incision is made into the side of a silver fir, its sap may be scraped off, heated, melted, mixed with wine and imbibed to provide relief from constipation in about 2 hours. The effect lasts for 24 hours.
foragables.warning: For the duration of its effect, imbibers of silver fir sap are unable to control their bowels.

foragables.name: Sindiluin
foragables.characteristics: This small plant is distinguishable by its small, blue flower that lasts for several weeks of the spring.
foragables.medicinalUses: Through a complicated process (whose secret skilled healers are reluctant to reveal), sildiluin may be made into a coagulant which, when applied to a wound, is capable of halting all bleeding.

foragables.name: Siran
foragables.characteristics: Siran superficially resembles garlic, but grows to a height of 1'. Its bulb is brownish, exuding an unmistakable onion-like smell if bruised.
foragables.medicinalUses: If peeled and eaten raw (something best attempted with the nose held), a siran clove restores I damaged organ to functionality within 1 hour. If more than 1 organ has been damaged, more cloves may be eaten (equal to the number of organs to be repaired). If an excess of cloves is ingested, this has no effect on the well-being of any of the organs.
foragables.warning:
One of the side effects of siran is a skin disease that manifests itself on the day after a clove is consumed. If several cloves have been ingested, the effect is cumulative (lasting 1 week/clove). The subject awakens to find his hands and face covered with large, greenish sores that leak a putrid-smelling pus (reduce Pr by 10%). The sores are not painful and disappear gradually toward the end of the week.

Some healers have a special salve to negate the stench, and may charge for it accordingly.

foragables.name: Siriena
foragables.characteristics: This short grass grows in tufts in sandy soils, never reaching a height of more than 1'. Only a few of its blades are green (the majority are a yellow-white), giving the general impression that it is on the verge of dying.
foragables.otherUses: If boiled in water and applied to an organic surface, siriena grass becomes a powerful preservative for up to 2 weeks,
foragables.warning: A great deal of effort is needed in order to get enough of the grass to preserve a person's body, and unfamiliarity with siriena can extend the task to several days. Though the grass does not lose its virtue when dried, the corpse may decompose into a bloated, scavenger-chewed, putrid mess.
foragables.cost: 70 gp/bushel (enough to preserve a man-sized surface)

foragables.name: Skull Cap
foragables.characteristics: This pallid white mushroom has an 18" diameter cap, smooth with black markings which, when viewed at a glance or from a distance, give it the appearance of a skull. The 2' stalk has a skirt-like ring half way up its length which emits a foul odour.
foragables.otherUses: Skull cap is a deadly ingestive poison whose virulence operates upon its victim for a full 24 hours before abating.
foragables.warning: The only antidotes for this toxin are some of the life-preserving herbs,

foragables.name: Slimy Gorkin
foragables.characteristics: This brownish fungus looks like a typical mushroom in shape (a 4" diameter convex or flat cap on a 2" high stalk). Its grey gills, covered with a slimy substance resembling mucus, descend to the stalk. Slimy gorkins tend to grow in large patches of several hundred individual fungi.
foragables.otherUses: This disgusting fungus may be eaten, though it leaves a great deal to be desired in terms of taste and texture.

foragables.name: Slird
foragables.characteristics: This short (10') citrus tree has triangle-shaped leaves. Its light green bark is perfectly smooth. Its fruit resembles a lemon, but it is bright red and extremely sweet. It loves lots of sun so it found on the edges of forests or in clearings.
foragables.otherUses: When ground to a pulp and allowed to ferment in an open stoneware container for a month, slird fruits decompose into a putrid, offensive mess which, if filtered and reduced in volume to a thick paste by boiling, becomes a fast-acting, circulatory poison (2nd level} that strikes its victim in 10-20 seconds and paralyses 1-6 extremities (head, genitals, hands, feet) for 1-100 days. A brew of sharag may remedy the effects of slird within 1-2 days.
foragables.warning: The stench of fermenting slird fruit is so noxious as to alert anyone passing within a 4% mile that foul deeds are afoot,

foragables.name: Slota
foragables.characteristics: Slota is both the name of a plant and the spider that inhabits it. The plant is a tall bush with long branches and few leaves; spiders build their webs here, using the natural framework of the plant to extend the size of their traps considerably, The slota spider is about the size of a man’s thumbnail, black with 8 brilliant red eyes, It does not fear Men, defending its web against anything it perceives to be a threat.
foragables.otherUses:
The venom of the slota spider is deadly. Since it is nearly impossible to extract, assassins simply grind up the entire arachnid. This poison must be administered by blade; contact or placing it in food have no effect. Once ingested (whether through weapon wound or spider sting), 10 minutes of total paralysis results. The victim’s condition
worsens until his lungs and heart stop (sometime within the next 24 hours). A paste made from toad’s glove and administered orally is rumoured to be capable of reversing the effects of slota, but no other antidote has ever been mentioned in folklore save the greater, lifegiving herbs of legend.
foragables.warning: Slota spiders are fast and aggressive, and care should be exercised by anyone wanting to make their own poison, especially if they are attempting to capture a spider alone.

foragables.name: Snapcane
foragables.characteristics:
Snapcane resembles a cluster of vines, except that its stems are divided into 3" long segments whose joints looks like knuckles. If broken, these stems make a loud snapping noise. The vines grow laterally along the ground. The small, bright green, oval-shaped leaves of the snapcane cluster only about the plant's centre. After the snow melts, these leaves sprout, each blossoming into a single yellow flower I week later. After yet another week, the snapcane releases its seeds on the wind and its flowers die, falling to the ground. Each seed sprouts into a tiny plant before the
snows return, arresting its growth until the next thaw. Only
plants 5 years and older produce annual flowers
foragables.medicinalUses: When ground up, snapcane stems may be used as part of the cure for the disease shutinis. A dried stem keeps for decades.

foragables.name: Snowbane
foragables.characteristics: This small herb has 2 thumb-sized leaves growing at its base, both taller than its stem. In early spring, even before the spring-melt, snowbane produces bright red flowers which last for much of the short growing season. It does not thrive in warmer climes or lower altitudes.
foragables.medicinalUses: When eaten, each snowbane leaf restores 2-10 hits, warming the consumer all over and enabling him to withstand (though not become impervious to) cold for 12 hours without heavy clothes. The subject still feels the chill, but it is easily dismissed and does not distract him or have its usual physiological effects. Snowbane leaves keep for 3 weeks after being picked.

foragables.name: Snowdragon
foragables.characteristics: This vine is a robust plant with a stem that grows as thick as a man’s thumb. It has only 4, claw-shaped leaves, each of which has 4 lobes ending in a curved point. Snowdragons can reach several feet in length and are not dormant when the snows come; on the contrary, they continue to grow and turn until they lie atop the drifts, their evergreen leaves splayed out like legs.
foragables.medicinalUses: A brewed mixture of snowdragon stem and true tarnas is said to cure the disease juth.

foragables.name: Sôrul Nut
foragables.characteristics: This medium (20') pine was originally native to cold, well-watered forests, later widely cultivated. The tree itself is attractive, often planted as an ornamental, and its soft wood is dark yellow.
foragables.medicinalUses: Its delicious nuts stabilise the enchantment of nur-oiolosse, and are prized as a delicacy in many cold to mild countries.
foragables.otherUses: Nut

foragables.name: Splayfoot
foragables.characteristics:
This beneficial plant grows among reeds deep within marshes. Its slender upright stalks are anchored Snowbane in the water by roots that rise as much as 1' above water level, The plant itself may stand 5-7’ tall, branching into delicate stalks with paper-thin, scalloped leaves and dangling, delicate, lavender-coloured flowers. When its seed-pods ripen
in mid-autumn, they take the shape of curved pea pods, like little green crescent moons hanging over the marshes. Each pod carries 3-4 shiny, black seeds.
foragables.otherUses: When mashed and mingled with any beverage, splayfoot goodwort seeds instil confidence and singleness of purpose into the hearts of the good and honest (+25); to evil folk or creatures of Darkness, the seeds bring on dizziness and confusion (-50) lasting 1-4 hours,

foragables.name: Stag's Purse
foragables.characteristics: This strange plant begins life as a vine that sprouts at the feet of deciduous trees, growing up the trunk and out onto the lower branches. There it begins to develop a brown, fuzzy bladder (about the size of a hog’s stomach) with a large, white flower, This “stag’s purse” hangs down from the tree and contains seeds, When touched with any force, it bursts into a shower of tiny, sticky seeds.
foragables.medicinalUses: If carefully split, its inward side placed against a burn caused by the poison silmiré, the purse eases suffering and speeds healing.

foragables.name: Stonelance
foragables.characteristics:
This plant has several large leaves (about the size of a man’s palm) growing near its base. A single round stalk (the thickness of a man’s thumb) rises from the midst of these leaves. In early summer, a purple flower appears on top of the stalk. For its length (1'), the stonelace stalk is as light as the lightest wood, but has the strength of iron. This
property lasts for years before the stem becomes brittle.
foragables.medicinalUses: If ground up and mixed with water, the stonelace flower forms a paste that reduces fever and cures colds. Its ground leaves are part of the cure for the disease vemék.
foragables.otherUses: The stalk has been put to a thousand uses, from sword handles to hinge pins to anything else where its strength may be put to good use.
foragables.warning: Though they possess the strength of iron, they do not have its hardness: prison bars made of the stalks could be cut through with a dagger (or even with a set of healthy teeth and a lot of patience),

foragables.name: Stout Heart
foragables.characteristics: This small, twisted, purple/mauve fungus commonly grows in caverns that are fairly dry.
foragables.otherUses: Extensive consumption of stout-heart (more than 3 pieces in 24 hours) increases a Dwarf’s Constitution indefinitely (to its potential maximum).
foragables.warning: Stout-heart eaters of all other races must make an RR each time they consume the fungus. A failed roll means their stomach rejects it with severe vomiting.

foragables.name: Strawthumb
foragables.characteristics: This small fungus resembles a short, yellow mushroom with no cap, only a stalk. It normally grows to a height of only 1" and may be flecked with black dots along its length.
foragables.otherUses: Ingestion of 1 strawthumb increases the consumer's Strength (+5) for 10 minutes.
foragables.warning:
Strawthumb leaves a very particular and extremely unpleasant aftertaste in the mouth. After the first dose, the consumer is unable to bring himself to eat another within the
same 24 hour period, (If he does, he is plagued by horrible nightmares for 2 nights — phantasms so terrifying that he cannot eat another strawthumb for 30 days.) None of the dreams are remembered upon waking, yet all return as soon as sleep is sought again.

foragables.name: Suranie
foragables.characteristics: This small bush prefers to grow along the edge of moving water, growing to a height of 5'. It has groups of 5, perfectly round leaves, joined by clusters of small red berries after the summer solstice.
foragables.medicinalUses: So pungent is its odour that, if crushed under the nose of an unconscious person, a suranie berry acts as smelling salts, startling them back to wakefulness. The berries keep for months before drying out and losing their potency.
foragables.otherUses: If a bundle of suranie branches are tied together, they may be waved about the head to stave off flying insects.
foragables.warning: If a suranie berry happens to be crushed while being carried in some pack or pouch, that container retains its powerful smell for 1 month, advertising its bearer to all noses downwind of it (50' radius).

foragables.name: Sweetstar
foragables.characteristics: This bush has woody, brown stems and short, waxy leaves that are as round as they are long, giving them the appearance of small, green balls. Its fruit, which appears in late summer, is yellow (about the size of a man’s thumb) and star-shaped. Its sweet, jelly-like pulp is filled with small, black seeds
foragables.medicinalUses: When scraped off from a small area of its stem, ground and boiled in water, sweetstar bark sends its imbiber into a deep sleep from which nothing can wake him. Slumber is induced within 1 minute of the final swallow. With respect to recuperation and healing, it is said that 1 night of such sleep is equal to 1 week in bed.
foragables.otherUses: Sweetstar fruits are delicious when baked and served in their own skins.

foragables.name: Sweet Sorrel
foragables.characteristics: This attractive little plant has trefoil leaves and white, bell-like flowers. It grows to a height of 1' and prefers the shade.
foragables.medicinalUses: When heated in boiling water for a few minutes so that their steam can be released, sweet sorrel leaves, when inhaled, act as an antidote to most poisonous vapors. It also relieves lung-spasms brought on by other causes, such as the poison kennesank.

foragables.name: Swigmakrîl
foragables.characteristics: This is a desert cactus that grows to around 3' tall. large white blossoms open at night to catch any moisture.
foragables.medicinalUses: On ingesting the flowers, either raw or infused in a tea is a relaxant allowing the imbiber to take double the normal concussion hits before passing out, but death still occurs at the same point. This effect lasts for 1-2 hours.

foragables.name: Swûth
foragables.characteristics: Swûth is a tall plant of the hemp family,often thought to be related to galenas, originally native to humid, tropical ocean shores, later cultivated.
foragables.otherUses: When dried, swûth leaves can be smoked like tobacco. The invisible swûth smoke relaxed the user for 1-10 minutes.

foragables.name: Tarfeg
foragables.characteristics: This tree grows up to 20' tall with a single straight trunk.  It has dark green, oval leaves about 2" long, pale greenish-white flowers with eight petals about 1" wide, and yellow-brown nuts.
foragables.medicinalUses: Ingesting the edible flowers repair sprains in 2-20 rounds.

foragables.name: Tarnas
foragables.characteristics: True farnas is striking when it flowers, possessing a 2' green stem surrounded by fern-like fronds and topped by a single white bloom like a large orchid. Each individual tarnas plant grows in accord with its own, idiosyncratic time-clock, so that plants in various stages of development may be seen growing side by side.
foragables.medicinalUses: When boiled in water, the bulb of this plant produces a potion capable of restoring any organ damage.
foragables.warning: Although sometimes found near flowing specimens, there is no guarantee that tarnas bulbs are readily available. Armchair herbalists sometimes confuse them with hopper mushrooms.

foragables.name: Tartella
foragables.characteristics: Tartella is a plant that looks like pipeweed, but is much smaller, It has blood-red edges to its small leaves; its stem is brownish-green.
foragables.otherUses: When its dried leaves are smoked, this much-abused herb induces a powerful euphoria for 1-10 hours. A refined version of tartella, known as tartec, is 4x stronger than regular Tartella, so that only ½ of the normal dosage is necessary to produce the same result. If a whole dose of tartec is taken, however, it induces a deeper state of euphoria, further removing the user from reality (-20 to all stats for 2-15 hours).
foragables.warning:
The tartella user become resistant to the drug's effect after 2-5 doses, such that an ever-increasing dosage is needed to achieve its euphoric effect. Tartella is also extremely addictive: more than 2 doses in a 3-day period precipitates withdrawal symptoms unless another dose is taken within the next 72 hours. Symptoms include severe nausea, headaches and chills (and seizures, if the addiction is long-term).

While under the effect of the drug, the user is weakened and out of touch with reality (-10 to all stats; most activity requiring concentration, such as fighting or casting spells, becomes impossible or, at best, clumsy). A full dose of tartec can result in damage to the reasoning centers of the brain. Addiction to tartec occuts more rapidly than normal tartella, and withdrawal are more severe. After each full dose, there is a 90% chance that the user’s Re permanently decreases by 1. Of course, the user is too impaired to realize the long-term damage.

foragables.name: Taynaga
foragables.characteristics: This evergreen is distinguished by the minute veins of orange lichen growing near the base of its trunk, It reaches a height of over 30’ and has very small cones, each the size of a pea. Its needles grow in groups of 3, each pointed with a soft barb.
foragables.medicinalUses: When dried, reduced to a powder and mixed with water, taynaga bark may be used to sterilise contaminated objects. It also neutralises the poison jegga and anything touched by it.
foragables.otherUses: When internalised (whether by ingestion or envenomed wound), taynaga acts as a poison, inflicting 5-50 hits within 6-12 minutes, If ingested before this is fully inflicted, rosecreepet powder negates any further damage. The victim writhes on the ground, complaining of a fire under their skin.

foragables.name: Telek
foragables.characteristics: Telek is identical in appearance to the strawberry plant, but its leaves are smooth rather than jagged. In spring, it produces small white berries in clusters of about a dozen.
foragables.medicinalUses: If consumed, a handful of telek berries restores 3-30 hits of cold-related injury; if crushed and spread on frostbitten flesh, it miraculously heals all damage within 10 rounds. Telek juice keeps for up to a month. A side effect is that the consumer becomes thirsty.

foragables.name: Temsanc
foragables.characteristics: This delicate mushroom is only 2" tall with a tiny stem and cap. It is white and grows in bunches of about a dozen.
foragables.otherUses: The essence of temsanc exaggerates the effects of alcoholic beverages. Undetectable when dissolved in liquor, it accelerates the onset of drunkenness and intensifies its subsequent effects (3x normal).

foragables.name: Terbas
foragables.characteristics: Terbas is a low shrub (2") with large leaves (each the size of a man’s hand) covered with small, white spots.
foragables.medicinalUses: When wrapped tightly around an affected body part and doused with hot water, terbas leaves hasten the healing of nerve damage (2x normal rate). The leaves must remain in place for 2 hours before replaced with fresh ones until the damage is healed to a suitable level.

foragables.name: Thurl
foragables.characteristics:
This herb is identical in appearance to a small onion plant, except that thurl leaves are red-tipped. It possesses a single, underground bulb (much like that of garlic).

One of thurl’s “slang-names” (actually a famous saying) recalls the anger of an ancient Hillman chieftain whose rather inept leech would insistently treat him after battles with a long drought of wine seasoned with thurl clove, After several weeks of suffering under this unpleasant remedy, the chieftain is reported to have said “Mae e’n gwneud fy mod i'n glaf. Lladdwch fe.” (“He makes me sick—kill him.”) To this day the Hillmen jokingly refer to thurl by this epithet.
foragables.medicinalUses: When eaten on an empty stomach, a thurl clove restores 1-4 hits; when consumed under any other circumstances, it provokes startlingly violent vomiting (of which thurl’s many names are onomatopoetic evocations).

foragables.name: Toad's Glove
foragables.characteristics:
This small fungus grows on dead things in the steamy environment where fate takes its daily due. When a dead animal or person hits the forest floor, it begins to decompose rapidly; insects, scavenging animals and opportunistic fungi make their way quickly to the corpse and begin to feed. Within 12 hours of death, toad’s glove spores settle
themselves on the flesh and sprout in another 2 hours. 6 hours later, the tiny, brown and black, wart-like fungus is mature and already making more spores. By the time the corpse is reduced to a skeleton (1 week later), dozens of generations of this fungus have come and gone.
foragables.medicinalUses: The ground up, small, wart-like body of the mature fungus is rumoured to be one of the only antidotes able to counteract the poison slota. Toad’s glove keeps for up to 1 week before losing its virtue, but healers have learned how to keep a toad’s glove culture active (sometimes for years) by storing it in a closed container with rotting meat.
foragables.cost: 125 gp/dose, because of the difficulty of keeping it alive

foragables.name: Traitor's Goblet
foragables.characteristics: This fungus resembles an urn, 1' in height and 8" in diameter, Its exterior appears to be covered with black hair, whereas its innards are smooth and dull brown of hue. An overhanging lip serves as the cap of this strange mushroom, which grows as a solitary individual.
